source.title: Large-scale photonic natural language processing
source.authors: C. Valensise; I. Grecco; D. Pierangeli; C. Conti

record.tranche_reason: The study varies the number of readout channels and training examples and reports test accuracy around the interpolation threshold, but uses a photonic extreme learning machine rather than the original deep-network methods.
record.gate_note: The text reports test-accuracy curves against channel count and training-set size, including a dip at the interpolation threshold. Figures 3A-C also report accuracy saturation as channel count increases. Figure 3D and Figure 4 comparisons do not isolate the claimed peak near the interpolation threshold, so they are not recorded as rows. No epoch-wise sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps the readout size M of a photonic extreme learning machine (random optical features with a ridge readout) on IMDb. It reports a test-accuracy dip at M = Ntrain and recovery beyond it. This is a new model class and hardware setting, not a deep network, so it bears on V4 and not on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors report what they call the first observation of double descent on photonic hardware: an accuracy dip at M = Ntrain with recovery beyond it. They argue that over-parametrization lets the device reach the same optimal accuracy (0.77) with far fewer training points.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps feature/channel count and training-set size and evaluates test accuracy around interpolation, but uses an optical extreme learning machine with ridge-regression readout on IMDb rather than the original deep-network settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The location of the accuracy dip moves with training-set size. For Fig. 3, the onset of saturation changes with input-space size.
record.code_released: Codes developed within the research are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
record.problems: Evidence is from one photonic model and one classification dataset. The curves are reported in figures without uncertainty estimates; the sample-size sweep at the threshold varies M and Ntrain jointly. No epoch-wise results are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3(D) varies the training-test split in the reported over-parameterized settings, not near the interpolation threshold. Figure 4 compares selected parameter-count regimes and other algorithms but does not report a size sweep or the double-descent shape.

untested.parts: No deep network is swept in size; the CNN in Fig. 4 is a fixed benchmark only.
No reported increase in samples at fixed model size near the threshold; Fig. 3D is far into the over-parametrized regime.
Only one model class (photonic ELM) on one dataset, with no uncertainty estimates.
No label-noise manipulation and no multiple peaks. The effect of regularization on the peak is not reported.
No effective-parameter re-expression of the curve.

missing.what: The ridge parameter λ was varied over [1e-4, 1e-2]; the text says it does not considerably influence test accuracy. Whether the peak survives tuned regularization is not shown.
Text states the 0.77 maximum in Fig. 2A lies in the under-parametrized region; the over-parametrized recovery does not exceed it at Ntrain ≈ 1.2e4.
missing.locator: Observation of the photonic double descent, Fig. 2(A)

record.verdict_notes: The model is a random-feature or kernel-like ELM, closer in kind to the random-features settings of Belkin et al. than to deep networks; hence V4 and not V1. All evidence is figure-only, with no error bars and a single dataset. Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 do not show the peak.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests readout-channel size in one photonic model on IMDb, not size scaling in deep networks generally.
The joint sweep varies channel count and training-set size; it does not isolate a training-set-size increase while holding model size fixed near the threshold.
The study tests the curve in one photonic extreme learning machine; it does not test it across a range of model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study does not test noise dependence, multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not re-express the curve using an effective parameter count or test whether that makes it an ordinary U-shape.
